help.stdout:
Out-of-core graph algorithms over DataFusion

Usage: graphframes <COMMAND>

Commands:
  page-rank          PageRank via Pregel
  wcc                Weakly connected components via randomized contraction
  mis                Maximal independent set (Ghaffari's algorithm)
  kcore              k-core (coreness) decomposition
  hyperanf           HyperANF approximate neighbourhood function
  shortest-path      Multi-source shortest paths
  pic                Power Iteration Clustering (Lin & Cohen 2010; Spark MLlib-inspired)
  mllib              Raw (graph-free) machine-learning algorithms
  fastrp             FastRP (Fast Random Projection) vertex embeddings
  fastrp-clustering  Graph clustering: FastRP embeddings (unit norm) + K-Means
  classical-lp       Classical Label Propagation (CDLP)
  help               Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -h, --help     Print help
  -V, --version  Print version

wcc_help.stdout:
Weakly connected components via randomized contraction

Usage: graphframes wcc [OPTIONS] --vertices <VERTICES> --edges <EDGES> --output <OUTPUT> --seed <SEED>

Options:
      --vertices <VERTICES>
          Path (or URI) to the vertices file or directory.
          
          Vertex-id column (`id` by default; override with `--id-col-name`). Int64, or a string column that is remapped to synthetic Int64 ids (the originals are kept in an `origin_id` column). Extra attribute columns are allowed but ignored on the Int64 path.

      --edges <EDGES>
          Path (or URI) to the edges file or directory.
          
          Source/destination columns (`src`/`dst` by default; override with `--src-col-name` / `--dst-col-name`). Int64, or string columns that are remapped to synthetic Int64 ids.

      --output <OUTPUT>
          Output directory as a `file://` URI, e.g. `file:///tmp/out/`.
          
          The result is always written as parquet regardless of `--format`; parent directories are created automatically.

      --format <FORMAT>
          Input file format for `--vertices` and `--edges`.
          
          Parquet by default. `csv` / `json` use DataFusion's default schema inference and parsing options.
          
          [default: parquet]
          [possible values: parquet, csv, json]

      --id-col-name <ID_COL_NAME>
          Name of the vertex-id column in the input; renamed to the library's `id`
          
          [default: id]

      --src-col-name <SRC_COL_NAME>
          Name of the edge source column in the input; renamed to the library's `src`
          
          [default: src]

      --dst-col-name <DST_COL_NAME>
          Name of the edge destination column in the input; renamed to `dst`
          
          [default: dst]

      --symmetrize
          Symmetrize the input graph after loading (add the reverse of every edge).
          
          Useful for algorithms defined on undirected graphs when the input stores each edge only once (LDBC undirected datasets). Off by default: some algorithms (e.g. PageRank) are only defined on directed graphs, and the per-algorithm decision belongs to the caller.

      --weighted
          Keep the edge weight column in the graph.
          
          Currently no algorithm consumes edge weights, but keeping the column makes the loaded `GraphFrame` ready for weighted algorithms (e.g. SSSP).

      --weight-col-name <WEIGHT_COL_NAME>
          Name of the edge weight column; only used with `--weighted`
          
          [default: weight]

      --max-memory <MAX_MEMORY>
          DataFusion spill-pool memory limit, e.g. `4G` or `512M`.
          
          A command-line value takes precedence over the environment variable.
          
          [env: GRAPHFRAMES_MAX_MEMORY=]
          [default: 4G]

      --num-workers <NUM_WORKERS>
          Parallelism (= DataFusion `target_partitions`).
          
          A command-line value takes precedence over the environment variable.
          
          [env: GRAPHFRAMES_NUM_WORKERS=]
          [default: 2]

      --checkpoint-dir <CHECKPOINT_DIR>
          Base working directory for checkpoints and DataFusion spill files.
          
          Relative paths resolve against the current directory; the directory and its `checkpoints/` and `df-spill/` subdirectories are created if missing. A command-line value takes precedence over the environment variable.
          
          [env: GRAPHFRAMES_WORKDIR=]
          [default: gf_workdir]

      --max-temp-file <MAX_TEMP_FILE>
          Upper bound on the total size of DataFusion's temporary spill directory, e.g. `200G`.
          
          A command-line value takes precedence over the environment variable.
          
          [env: GRAPHFRAMES_MAX_TEMP_FILE=]
          [default: 200G]

      --seed <SEED>
          Random seed for the per-iteration affine hashes

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')
